extracted.intended_audience: researchers, engineers, and program managers preparing or evaluating DARPA research program proposals
extracted.subtask_description: A short checklist of eight questions (the Heilmeier Catechism) used to evaluate proposed research programs, covering objectives, current practice, novelty, impact, risks, cost, schedule, and measurable milestones. Intended to make proposers and reviewers think through context, resources, and success criteria.

rubrics_metrics.name: What are you trying to do?
rubrics_metrics.description: Articulate your objectives using absolutely no jargon.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State the project's goals clearly and simply so a non-specialist can understand the objective; avoid technical jargon. This is the opening framing question that defines the problem and intended outcome.

rubrics_metrics.name: How is it done today, and what are the limits of current practice?
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe the current state-of-the-art approaches and their limitations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain existing methods or technologies, identify shortcomings or capability gaps, and show why current practice is inadequate relative to the stated objective.

rubrics_metrics.name: What is new in your approach and why do you think it will be successful?
rubrics_metrics.description: Explain the novel aspects of the proposed approach and provide reasons to believe it will work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clarify the innovation or new idea, the underlying rationale, supporting preliminary data or theory if available, and why this approach overcomes current limitations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Who cares? If you are successful, what difference will it make?
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify stakeholders and the potential impact or benefits if the project succeeds.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain who will value the results (e.g., military users, industry, science) and articulate the practical or strategic difference the success will produce.

rubrics_metrics.name: What are the risks?
rubrics_metrics.description: List technical, programmatic, and other risks that could prevent success.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide a frank assessment of uncertainties, failure modes, and key assumptions; indicate how risks will be monitored, mitigated, or de-risked during the program.

rubrics_metrics.name: How much will it cost?
rubrics_metrics.description: Estimate the total cost required to execute the program.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Give realistic budgeting estimates tied to tasks and phases; justify major cost items and explain cost drivers or contingencies.

rubrics_metrics.name: How long will it take?
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide an expected schedule or timeline for the work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State the program duration, key phases and timing, and any dependencies that affect schedule; align time estimates with milestones and resource needs.

rubrics_metrics.name: What are the mid-term and final “exams” to check for success?
rubrics_metrics.description: Define measurable mid-term and final tests, demonstrations, or metrics that will indicate progress and success.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specify objective success criteria, performance metrics, prototypes, demonstrations, or decision points that allow reviewers to judge whether the program is meeting goals.
